findings.reason: adopting object identity deletes the binary-detection heuristic, the bytes read and the docstring rule from §1's deliverable entirely, and changes what the test must assert.
findings.text: §1 prescribes reading blob content as bytes and picking "the narrowest test for binary" (a NUL byte or a failed UTF-8 decode) inside `_show`, but a content comparison is unnecessary: `git rev-parse <revision>:<path>` returns the blob's object id without decoding anything, and the module already resolves object names that way (`merge.py:125`, `merge.py:264-265`), so a binary path can be compared by blob identity with no bytes read, no binary heuristic and no new docstring rule — the repo moreover already reads git output in bytes where content really is still wanted (`reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:922-947`, `git diff --binary` with `capture_output=True` and no `text=True`), which is the pattern §1 should cite if a byte read is genuinely wanted

findings.reason: the new cases belong in the file the plan already gates on (one harness, one revision of the fixture) rather than in two files that re-derive it, and naming the harness shortens both done-when blocks.
findings.text: the plan's two new test files (`tests/test_a_landing_reads_binary_files.py`, `tests/test_a_failed_land_exits_nonzero.py`) each rebuild a temporary origin-and-checkout repository with every environment-resolved directory redirected, which this file already provides: `_write_origin_and_checkout` at `tests/test_one_call_lands_a_run.py:34`, the `crew complete --land` CliRunner driver `_complete_land` at `tests/test_one_call_lands_a_run.py:134`, the shared git helper `tests/helpers/git.py:12`, and an existing test over exactly the functions §1 changes at `tests/test_one_call_lands_a_run.py:236`; the same plan already names this file in both gates, so the census is three reused mechanisms across two node briefs, not one drift-prone copy per section

findings.reason: the plan must state the per-path kind in the `survived` payload (or one place that owns the text/binary decision and returns it), otherwise the landing record reports a check that did not run.
findings.text: the binary branch is invisible in the module's own report: `land()` builds `survived` as `{"checked": bool(markers), "paths": sorted(markers), "markers": sum(introduced + removed)}`, and a path judged by blob identity contributes zero introduced and zero removed markers, so a landing whose only reviewed change is binary reports `checked: true, markers: 0` — a record that §2's own report leans on to state that the land step succeeded, and that cannot be told apart from a check that inspected nothing; the plan adds the decision at `merge.py:280` and `merge.py:305` without saying where it lives or what the report says about it

findings.reason: the exception-to-refusal mapping (type, message, resume command, exit status) should be one owner — a helper beside `MergeError` in `reckon/crew/merge.py`, which the five sites call — or §2 must each add a catch that drifts from the others the first time one changes.
findings.text: the mapping from a merge failure to a refusal is duplicated across five sites in one module and §2 extends it by adding more sites rather than naming an owner: `crew_merge`'s `except merge.MergeError` at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:74` (with `MergePushOutstandingError` at :74-76), the promoted-land handler at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2449`, `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2475`, `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2485`, and the release-step push handler at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2524` (currently `pragma: no cover`); the plan names only two of these (`_land_a_promoted_run` and the `crew merge` verb) and asks each to catch "any other exception" separately

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §1 spreads one decision (text or binary, and what "unchanged" means for it) across two functions in `reckon/crew/merge.py` (`change_markers` at :280 and `surviving_change_refusals` at :305) without naming where the decision lives, and leaves the module's own public report (`merge.py:652`, the `survived` block) unable to say a path was judged by blob identity, so the landing record cannot distinguish a binary check from a no-op.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the merge-exception-to-refusal mapping is already duplicated across five sites in `reckon/crew_run_commands.py` and §2 adds a per-site catch at two of them rather than extending one owner for the mapping.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1969, cli_options 394, mcp_views 19, refusal_families 23; neither section adds a public definition, a CLI option, an MCP view or a new refusal name, so there is no family entry for a section to retire or merge.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites `reckon/crew/merge.py`'s `_show`, `change_markers` and `surviving_change_refusals` by line, so it read the code it extends, but it did not search for a mechanism that already answers "did this path's content change" without decoding it (`git rev-parse <rev>:<path>`, already used in `reckon/crew/merge.py:125`), nor for the repo's existing bytes-mode git read (`reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:922`), and its two new test files rebuild a temporary-repository harness that `tests/test_one_call_lands_a_run.py:34` already carries.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §1 extends `_show`/`_run` in place inside `reckon/crew/merge.py` and adds no parallel reader or second landing path; §2 extends the existing land-step and `crew merge` handlers rather than wrapping them in a layer.
